Both demonstrated R1 cost blocks are closed at this new head: command packets are chunked, and a retained-exited pane no longer causes an unchanged-prefix launch storm that starves the live suffix. Source and exact-head real-adapter CI support the closure. The old BLOCK at1c998e7 remains evidence about that old head, not clearance or a block for this fixed head. No new normal-use resource-cost blocker is established here; fleet AFTER is still owed.

Launch-bound verification:
- detach_chunk_len uses the same ten arguments as detach_args, adds each argument's UTF-8 byte length plus its NUL and the2-byte inter-pair separator, and caps normal chunks at8192 argument bytes. This addresses the former roughly17KiB packet rejection. It guarantees at least one pair; the budget statement here concerns canonical short tmux pane IDs, not arbitrary oversized caller strings.
- Healthy launch count is greedy BYTE packing, not a universal ceil(P/130). Example constant ID widths from the actual pair strings: %0 fits143 pairs, %12345 fits126, %4294967295 fits109. All give2 chunks for145 extant owned taps; approximately130 is a useful typical-width estimate. A300-real-pane fixture now requires2-4 distinct launches and clears every pipe/marker/sink.
- Let P be the initially listed owned pending entries and B the batch-write attempts. A successful chunk is never resent: attached remnants are only read/polled, then completed or returned as errors. On failure, an observed vanished chunk entry is removed, or the first still-attached chunk entry is failed/removed; completed/gone entries are also removed. A verify failure aborts the remainder. Every continuing write round strictly decreases pending, so B<=P. There is no unchanged pending-list resend loop.
- The live/exited/live real-adapter test now asserts exactly2 distinct launches, both live taps detached and the exited pane's retained marker/sink and named error. The single exited-pane wrapper asserts exactly1 launch/Err. This replaces the former34/46-launch failure witnesses, not merely lowers the time taken to return the same failure.
- The bound is on the counted tmux.pipe-pane detach taps WRITE site, not all processes during stop. Normal reads use the retained control client; read Fork/startup/replacement paths can add other launches. With B write rounds and W convergence re-reads, snapshot calls are normally1+B+W. No new steady tick/per-seat launch is added.
- Scoped snapshot parsing, argument construction, ownership/result checks, pending-vector removal/retains and sink unlink work remain. Snapshot cost follows adapter-scope panes N; vector work follows remaining P across B rounds. A linear write-count cap is not a blanket linear CPU/IO bound, especially with many failing panes.
- The global2s grace starts after initial snapshot/ownership work and is checked before another write and during read convergence. Command::output and reads can outlast it; it remains a convergence grace, not a hard child/phase wall-time bound. Polling after success sleeps25ms and re-reads only, not rewrites.

- The1c998e7->23e4d369 main merge does not change the reviewed tmux detach implementation or pane-observer implementation (exact file comparisons passed).
